decision.recommended_next_task: Build a source-current coverage packet for release-conditioned cross-asset prediction before authorizing inference: official CPI/GDP/FOMC release text and vintage fields, joined to separately licensed ETF prices with a horizon fixed after document availability.
decision.reason: Economic report composition and policy language give interpretation nodes substantive evidence. Precise release headers prevent day-only news admission from becoming a fictitious intraday clock. Existing AAPL daily extrapolation is not the required ETF/sector task.
decision.first_falsifiable_question: At08:45 America/New_York after scheduled08:30 CPI/GDP releases, can a fixed interpretation→forecast graph improve later open-to-close relative returns across a frozen ETF universe versus numeric-only and report-headline-only controls? For14:00 FOMC, use a separately frozen next-session horizon; do not pool incompatible clocks.
not_ready: No licensed ETF price source with audited event/execution clock admitted in this pass.
No prediction-market historical bid/ask depth or executable-fill evidence established.
Polymarket data redistribution and AI-use terms not fully established; code MIT does not license all data.
Two macro release families and one Fed market example establish join mechanics, not study coverage, balanced outcomes, independence or performance.
decision.fallback_question: Before Fed releases, does prior official macro composition and a fixed history of market prices improve probability forecasts of the rate decision over the latest supplied market price? Use Brier/log scoring on event groups; do not call this a trading return backtest.
decision.fallback_limits: The inspected no-change contract was already priced96.15–98.95%; rare decisions and small meeting counts can make this a weak learning task. Require a full predefined calendar and retain missing history, all outcomes and failed forecasts.
